description: Saskatoon gathered public input for its Climate Action Strategy.
Engagement included newcomers, Indigenous groups, and businesses.
The full strategy will be presented for approval in August.

chips.text: Received as information
Committee encouraged to review the forthcoming strategy for equity considerations.
Newcomers engaged through Global Gathering Place and Saskatchewan Intercultural Association.
New strategy will supersede the low emissions community plan and corporate adaptation strategy.
Concerns raised about shifting climate action costs to low-income individuals and small businesses.
Public concerned about climate impacts, specifically wildfire smoke.

description: New Coming Home Centre will support Indigenous women, girls, Two-Spirit people.
Centre provides a safe, culturally grounded space for ceremonies.
Lease for the Centre's office space was approved.

chips.text: Received as information
Parking program saves Indigenous families $22.50 daily per vehicle for court visits.
Councillor noted the importance of the Auntie Advocate and the Coming Home Centre as the next phase.
Auntie Advocate Swiftwolfe spoke on behalf of Indigenous families and community members.
Parking program has supported 54 Indigenous families attending court proceedings.

description: Funds SamosaFest with $1,500 for the Saskatchewan Intercultural Association.
Reduced funding from $2,000 to extend budget for future sponsorships.
Event access is free; $15 fee only for meals.

chips.text: Approved
Committee debated funding amount and supporting ticketed events with meal costs.
Staff comment noted previous non-support for ticketed events.
